_meta: FIELD REPORT (the discovery-mode gap, wave 2 of 3): mid-project learning outdated a plan's topology — only one phase still made sense, but the agent said 'I can't run P4 alone, heartbeat is designed to run these sequentially'. Mechanically half-right: a parked predecessor deliberately does not satisfy a downstream gate_entry (fail-closed, by design), and the only way to cut the dependency was a hand edit of dag.json that agents refuse as unblessed. The dag IS the editable plan — `hb detach` makes the edit LOUD, attributed, reversible and reviewed, exactly as `hb regate` (wave 1, v1.37.0) did for criteria revision. DESIGN: `hb detach <PHASE|GATE> <reason…>` (python: --reason; the park/regate arg-style precedent; park-style resolution — a phase id, or the gate_exit that identifies it) retracts the phase's DEPENDENCY CLAIM: sets gate_entry to null and records {detached_from: <the old gate_entry>, detached_reason, detached_by: HB_ACTOR, detached_at} on the phase, appending an audit-only phase_detached {phase, from, reason} event — attribution in the log (the regate-declare precedent), with the read-modify-write under the write lock (the park lost-update refuter catch, baked in from the start). `hb reattach <PHASE|GATE>` restores gate_entry from detached_from, clears the detach fields, appends audit-only phase_reattached. REFUSALS (declare): empty reason; HB_ACTOR unset/'unknown'; unknown id; gate_entry already null (with a distinct message when detach fields are present: already detached — reattach first); phase already COMPLETE (nothing to unlock — retracting a satisfied dependency is archaeology, not planning). REFUSALS (reattach): not detached; detached_from names a gate that is not BOTH defined in dag.gates AND some phase's gate_exit (round-1 refuter: 'defined' alone still restores the lint error 'gate_entry is no phase's gate_exit — phase locked forever', a resolver brick; the lint shape rule for detached_from requires the same) — fix the dag first. RESOLVER/TICK/EXECUTORS: no changes — a null gate_entry already means unlocked; detach deliberately REUSES that semantic (that is the whole point: the mechanism is one field, the feature is the loudness around it). THE WEASEL VECTOR, decided allow-but-loud, with the warning PREDICATE defined PER-CHANNEL (round-1 refuter: 'any recorded gate_failed' over-fires on healed gates; round-2 refuter: a MERGED last-verdict stream under-fires on the refuted predecessor's STEADY STATE, review_failed → gate_passed with the review still owed — the exact moment the doctrine forbids escaping): the warning fires iff, for the detached-from gate, (a) a LIVE gate_failed — one with no later gate_passed for that gate, OR (b) a LIVE review_failed — one with no later review_passed; a later gate_passed does NOT clear it, mirroring the projection's acceptance semantics (the review is still owed), OR (c) regateBlocks(gate) blocks, OR (d) unansweredRegate(events, gate), OR (e) staleRearm(events, gate) — the rearmed-but-not-re-verified window (decided as a full arm: doctor already calls that state STALE; detaching from it is escaping before re-verification). The log-truth lesson throughout: hand-cleared markers must not silently disarm the loudness. Detaching such a gate is ALLOWED (refutation-driven replanning legitimately happens exactly when predecessors are blocked; a refusal rule would kill the honest use), and the declare message then carries: 'the dependency claim is REMOVED, not satisfied — this does not unblock or accept <gate>; re-audit, and the reason is on record'. The doctrine line (dev docs this wave; the discovery how-to is wave 3): never detach to escape a blocked or revising predecessor — that is auto-weaken by topology; the reviewer reads detached_from + detached_reason in the dag. THE SUBTLE POINT (round-1 refuter: the first design was WRONG in its primary scenario): `hb changed <gate_exit>` and the constraint-author change list use `gate_entry || _start` as the base anchor, so a naive detach silently WIDENS the phase's change report to plan-start. A detached_from-anchor fallback does NOT fix it — acceptance anchors exist only at acceptance, so the motivating case (predecessor parked/blocked/refuted, never accepted) has no anchor and still widens to _start; and a predecessor accepted LATER snapshots a tree that already CONTAINS the detached phase's work, under-reporting or hiding it from the refuter, with the base silently shifting between two calls mid-review-cycle. DECIDED INSTEAD: the DECLARE writes a DETACH-TIME ANCHOR — anchors/_detach_<PHASE>.json via a DIRECT writeAnchor/write_anchor call (NOT tryAnchor: that helper is explicitly write-once for acceptance anchors, and following it would ship a stale anchor that lies on re-detach — a round-2 catch), the decision made inside the write lock, the tree hashed after release, a write failure warned loudly on stderr and never swallowed — and both runtimes' changed() resolve the base as gate_entry || the phase's detach anchor || _start. It is REWRITTEN by each successful declare (a re-detach after a reattach starts a new entry point; declare is refused while already detached, so successful declares serialize) and STAMPED with the declare's detached_at: changed() treats an anchor whose stamp mismatches the phase's live detached_at as MISSING (the post-lock hash of an older declare landing late must fall back loudly, never lie — a round-2 catch), and it is inert after reattach (gate_entry wins again). A detached phase whose anchor is missing OR stamp-mismatched falls back to _start and doctor's live-detach note says so ('no detach anchor — change reports widen to _start'). NAMESPACE: gate ids matching ^_start$ or ^_detach_ are a lint ERROR on both runtimes (the anchors/ namespace is reserved — an acceptance anchor for such a gate would collide), and the DECLARE refuses a phase id that fails the SAFE filename rule (the SAFE_GATE_ID charset — a phase id with / or .. must never reach path.join under anchors/); lint also errors when detach fields sit on a phase whose id fails that rule. Parity-cased (changed is a shared surface). SURFACING (DT2): hb report marks a detached phase line '⟂ detached from <gate> (by <actor>: <reason>)' on both runtimes (text render only, gone after reattach, absent when never detached — the regate-marker precedent incl. strip-clean guard lines); doctor NOTES a live detach (dependency removed — re-audit; appending 'no detach anchor — change reports widen to _start' when the anchor is missing) and NOTES the dag/log divergence in BOTH directions with LIVE-state semantics (the regate marker-sync lesson; round-2: the narrow 'no phase_detached event' wording missed the fail-OPEN restore): direction A — detach fields present while the log does not attest a LIVE detach (no phase_detached at all, OR the last one answered by a later phase_reattached: a dag restored from a mid-detach backup after the live flow reattached leaves the phase silently UNLOCKED, the dangerous direction); direction B — an unanswered phase_detached while the phase carries no detach fields (the backup-restore re-lock). NOTES, not problems: topology edits are legal plan edits and carry no acceptance-laundering risk, unlike a regate marker; the verb is the loud path, not the only path. LINT (both runtimes, parity-pinned): when detach fields are present — detached_from must be a non-empty string naming a gate that is DEFINED and some phase's gate_exit, detached_reason a non-empty string, detached_by a non-empty string, detached_at a non-empty string timestamp; partial/malformed field sets are errors; detach fields alongside a NON-null gate_entry are an error (a half-reattach). PROOF HYGIENE (mandated — the wave-1 pollution incident): every new proof script — tests/detach.sh AND tests/detach-surfacing.sh — carries the env-hygiene header verbatim (`unset HB_DIR PROJECT_DIR GATE G DAG_FILE EVENTS_FILE`) before any fixture work; BOTH gates' review prompts check it. UX + interplay lines for the docs (round-1 refuter): the declare output LEADS with 'detached <phase> from <detached_from>' (passing a gate id resolves it as a phase's gate_exit — the park precedent — so naming the ENTRY gate you mean to cut detaches the WRONG phase; the docs name the trap); detaching a PARKED phase succeeds but unlocks nothing until unpark (park's skip is independent of gate_entry); detaching a det-passed/review-owed phase is allowed (it is not COMPLETE) and moves no constraint grounding (its predecessor is complete, so the base anchor is unchanged); a pending regate on the predecessor never removes it from completed_phases (the projection ignores the marker) — detach changes nothing mechanically there beyond the warning. DELIBERATE NON-GOALS (deferred, not forgotten): no new tick PROTOCOL reason keys, no MCP tool (park/regate precedent), no audit-RULESET change (the parity-pinned verbatim ruleset stays byte-identical — DT2's proof asserts the audit verdict on a detached fixture is unchanged), no resolver change, and the discovery doctrine pieces — the skill's plan-to-the-knowledge-horizon rule, replanning-as-refutation-outcome, and the gated discovery how-to — are WAVE 3, authored after this verb's refutation rounds teach us what the doctrine text must say (the plan-to-the-horizon rule applied to itself). GUARD-MARKER CONTRACT (the regate selftest convention): every guard lives on strip-clean single lines carrying `detach-guard[: name]` markers — detach-lock, detach-validate, detach-warn, detach-anchor, reattach, changed-base, report, plus lint call-site markers — and the proofs' --selftest strips each from a COPY expecting the named check to go red for the RIGHT reason (the stripped file parses; the behavior re-opens). REFUTATION ROUND 1 (strong model): UNSOUND — 2 BLOCKING (the detached_from-anchor change base failed in the PRIMARY scenario — no anchor exists for a never-accepted predecessor, so the report widened to _start anyway, and a late acceptance made the base POSTDATE the work, under-reporting it and shifting mid-cycle → replaced by the DETACH-TIME ANCHOR above; the weasel-warning predicate was undefined/over-and-under-firing → made exact), 3 MAJOR (the env-hygiene header was not mandated — now mandated verbatim; the reattach/lint gate check needed 'defined AND some phase's gate_exit' or the restore re-bricks the resolver; the dag/log divergence note was one-directional — now both directions), 1 MINOR (the gate-id resolution trap, the park interplay, the lint timestamp wording, the review-owed/regated-predecessor doc lines — all folded). REFUTATION ROUND 2 (strong model, fresh): UNSOUND — 1 BLOCKING (the 'exact' predicate still under-fired on the refuted STEADY STATE, review_failed → gate_passed with the review owed — the merged last-verdict stream read; → the PER-CHANNEL arms above, with the steady-state fixture pinned, plus staleRearm decided as a full arm), 3 MAJOR (rewrite-per-declare had no fixture and the '_start pattern' pointer led to write-once tryAnchor → direct writeAnchor mandated + the re-detach fixture; divergence direction A missed the fail-OPEN restored-after-reattach case → live-state semantics + the second fixture; the hygiene mandate had not reached dt2a/GATE_DT2 → it has), 4 MINOR (the post-lock stale-hash lie → the detached_at STAMP with mismatch-as-missing; the _detach_/_start namespace + unsafe phase ids → reserved-name and safe-id lint/declare rules; the parity floor pinning one case while claiming three → all three pinned by name; GATE_DT1.desc naming the rejected design → fixed). ALL folded above.

tasks.title: Spec-first: author the detach proof (RED before dt1b/dt1c)
tasks.description: Author tests/detach.sh (prints DETACH-OK; --selftest prints DETACH-SELFTEST-OK with reason-checked guard strips) + failing pytest cases in py/tests/test_detach.py. DECLARE on BOTH runtimes (node trailing-words reason, python --reason; park-style resolution by phase id or gate_exit): sets gate_entry null, records {detached_from, detached_reason, detached_by, detached_at} with detached_from equal to the pre-detach gate_entry and detached_by = HB_ACTOR, appends audit-only phase_detached (state projection unchanged), all under ONE write lock — 6 concurrent detaches of the same phase: exactly one phase_detached event; a detach racing a park of ANOTHER phase: both edits survive (the wave-1 lost-update lesson). The proof carries the env-hygiene header VERBATIM (the wave-1 pollution incident). The DECLARE also writes the detach-time anchor anchors/_detach_<PHASE>.json via DIRECT writeAnchor (never tryAnchor — write-once would lie on re-detach), STAMPED with the declare's detached_at (decision in the lock, tree hashed after release; REWRITTEN by each successful declare; a failed write warns on stderr and never blocks the declare), and refuses a phase id failing the SAFE filename rule. The declare output LEADS with 'detached <phase> from <detached_from>'. REFUSALS, each loud with no event and no dag change: empty reason; unset/'unknown' HB_ACTOR; unknown id; gate_entry already null on a never-detached phase; already-detached (distinct message naming reattach); phase already complete. REATTACH: restores gate_entry from detached_from, clears all four fields, appends audit-only phase_reattached; refused when not detached and when detached_from is not BOTH a defined gate AND some phase's gate_exit (a bare 'defined' restore would recreate the lint 'phase locked forever' brick — fixture: delete the predecessor PHASE but keep its gate defined, reattach must refuse). WEASEL-VECTOR LOUDNESS, the per-channel predicate (arms a–e in _meta): fixtures for EACH arm and non-arm — a stale gate_failed healed by gate_passed detaches CLEAN; a review_failed-refuted predecessor WARNS; the refuted STEADY STATE (review_failed → the gate re-run and det-passed, review still owed) WARNS (the round-2 catch: a merged last-verdict stream goes clean here); a pending-regate predecessor WARNS; a hand-cleared regate marker (pending false by hand, log unanswered) WARNS; a rearmed-but-not-re-verified predecessor (gate_rearmed, no later provenanced pass) WARNS; a never-evaluated and a passed-clean predecessor detach clean — and the passed-clean fixture ALSO plants a live gate_failed and a live review_failed on a DIFFERENT gate, asserting the detach stays CLEAN (the per-gate filter discriminator: an unfiltered scan over-fires here and nowhere else). LINT RUNNABLES: the proof's lint fixtures include a reserved gate name (^_start$/^_detach_) and detach fields on an unsafe phase id, each a NON-EMPTY identical error on both runtimes. RESOLVER REUSE: after detach the phase's tasks join the ready set and the tick hands them out (next_task), with NO resolver/tick code change — assert by driving the tick on a locked-then-detached fixture. CHANGED-BASE (the detach anchor): (1) predecessor NEVER accepted (the motivating case) — after detach, `hb changed <gate_exit>` on BOTH runtimes reports against the detach anchor, NOT _start: the fixture plants pre-existing other-phase work that _start would wrongly include and asserts it is absent; (2) LATE ACCEPTANCE — the predecessor is accepted AFTER the detach (its acceptance anchor now contains the detached phase's work): the base stays the detach anchor, the phase's own work stays IN the report, and two `hb changed` calls straddling that acceptance agree (no mid-cycle base shift); (3) a detached phase whose anchor is MISSING (hand-deleted) falls back to _start; (4) after reattach, gate_entry wins again; (5) RE-DETACH after reattach with intervening work — the anchor is REWRITTEN and `hb changed` reports ONLY post-re-detach work (a write-once anchor would lie here); (6) a planted anchor whose stamp MISMATCHES the live detached_at is treated as missing (_start fallback — a late-landing stale hash must never lie). Wire into tests/run-tests.sh as the next free T group. RED first.

constraints.claim: Declare and reattach are attributed, locked, anchored and reversible on both runtimes: detach sets gate_entry null, records {detached_from = the pre-detach gate_entry, detached_reason, detached_by = HB_ACTOR, detached_at}, appends an audit-only phase_detached INSIDE the write lock (6 concurrent detaches yield exactly one event; a racing park of another phase loses no edit), writes the _detach_<PHASE> anchor via direct writeAnchor (rewritten per declare — proven by the re-detach fixture; stamped with detached_at; a failed write warns loudly, never silently), refuses an unsafe phase id, and the output leads with 'detached <phase> from <gate>'; reattach restores gate_entry, clears all four fields, appends phase_reattached, and refuses when not detached or when detached_from is not both a defined gate and some phase's gate_exit (the resolver-brick refusal); every declare refusal (no reason, no/unknown actor, unknown id, already-null entry, already detached, completed phase) is loud, event-free and dag-neutral.
constraints.violation: A detach or reattach mutates without the lock (a race loses an edit or doubles an event), omits or mis-records any of the four fields, succeeds on a refusal-ladder input, leaves state.json changed by the audit-only events, or reattach restores a dangling gate_entry.

constraints.claim: The weasel vector is allow-but-loud under the PER-CHANNEL predicate — the warning fires iff the detached-from gate has a live gate_failed (no later gate_passed), or a live review_failed (no later review_passed — a later gate_passed does NOT clear it: the refuted steady state warns), or regateBlocks blocks, or unansweredRegate attests, or staleRearm holds (so: a healed stale failure and a passed-clean predecessor detach CLEAN; refuted, re-run-but-unreviewed, revising, hand-cleared and rearmed-unverified predecessors ALL warn) — and the mechanism reuses existing semantics: the detached-from gate's own perimeter and acceptance rules are untouched; the detached phase's tasks join the ready set through the EXISTING null-gate_entry semantics — zero changes to the resolver, the tick's reason keys, the audit ruleset, or any MCP surface.
constraints.violation: The warning is absent on a live-failed, refuted (including the review_failed → gate_passed steady state), pending-regate, hand-cleared-marker or stale-rearmed predecessor, or present on a healed or never-evaluated one — or present when only a DIFFERENT gate's channel is live (the unfiltered-scan over-fire); a detach weakens the detached-from gate's own refusals in any way; or the diff touches resolver/tick/audit-ruleset/MCP code to make the unlock work.

constraints.claim: The change report stays honest through the DETACH ANCHOR: after a detach, `hb changed` on the phase's gate_exit reports against _detach_<PHASE> on both runtimes — never widening to _start and other phases' work (the never-accepted-predecessor fixture), never under-reporting the phase's own work, never shifting base when the predecessor is accepted later mid-cycle, REWRITTEN on re-detach (only post-re-detach work reported), and treating a stamp-mismatched anchor as missing — falling back to _start only then, and back to gate_entry after reattach; parity-cased (detach:changed-base, detach:cross, a non-empty detach:lint-malformed), and the lint shape rules (partial fields, fields with a non-null gate_entry, a detached_from that is not a defined gate AND some phase's gate_exit, an empty timestamp, a reserved gate name ^_start$/^_detach_, detach fields on an unsafe phase id) error identically and non-emptily on both runtimes.
constraints.violation: A detached phase's change list includes pre-detach other-phase work (_start widening), omits the phase's own work (a late-acceptance or stale/stamp-mismatched base), reports pre-re-detach work after a re-detach (a write-once anchor), or shifts between two calls straddling the predecessor's acceptance; the runtimes disagree on the base or any malformed record; a malformed record lints clean on both; or a parity case would stay green through such a divergence.

constraints.claim: Surfacing is loud, correct, text-only and non-invasive: both runtimes' reports mark a detached phase with the detached_from gate, actor and reason; the marker clears on reattach, is absent on never-detached projects and never appears in --json; doctor emits the detach NOTES with live-state semantics (the live detach with the anchor-missing suffix when it applies; direction A — fields without a LIVE log detach, covering both the no-event and the restored-after-reattach fail-open fixtures; direction B — the unanswered-event re-lock) and stays exit 0 when they are the only findings; and the audit ruleset is untouched — audit output on a detached fixture is byte-identical to the same fixture with the detach fields removed, on both runtimes.
constraints.violation: A detached fixture renders without the marker on either runtime, the marker survives reattach or leaks into --json, a detach note turns doctor's exit nonzero on its own, or audit output differs between the detached and stripped fixtures.

constraints.claim: Docs are current-state, honest and conformant: dev-plugin.md and dev-python.md describe the shipped verbs, refusal ladder, warning states, changed-base rule, doctor notes AND the report marker (the runtime docs, not just the test catalogue — the regate-wave lesson); the doctrine line is present verbatim in substance (never detach to escape a blocked or revising predecessor — auto-weaken by topology); dev-tests.md lists the new groups and proofs; parity-notes records the arg-style divergence, the three cases and the changed-base rule; and every backticked hb phrase in the four changed docs names a registered python subcommand.
